title: Tricyclic antidepressant (TCA) overdose
subject: toxicology
summary: TCA overdose causes coma, seizures, hypotension and sodium channel blockade with QRS widening. Give sodium bicarbonate 1 to 2 mEq/kg IV boluses for QRS above 100 ms, arrhythmia or hypotension, targeting pH 7.45 to 7.55; treat seizures with benzodiazepines; avoid physostigmine, flumazenil, phenytoin and class IA or IC antiarrhythmics.

sections.title: Recognise
items: Severe toxicity develops within the first few hours: anticholinergic features (tachycardia, mydriasis, dry skin, urinary retention, delirium), then coma, seizures, hypotension and arrhythmias.
The reported ingested dose is unreliable; the ECG predicts risk better than drug levels.
ECG danger signs: QRS above 100 ms (seizure risk) and above 160 ms (ventricular arrhythmia risk), terminal R wave in aVR above 3 mm, right axis deviation of the terminal QRS, Brugada-like pattern.
Common agents in India: amitriptyline, imipramine, dothiepin (dosulepin), nortriptyline, clomipramine.

sections.title: Immediate management
items: ABC; continuous ECG monitoring and a 12-lead ECG on arrival, repeated serially. Check glucose and a blood gas.
Intubate early for reduced consciousness, seizures or haemodynamic instability. After intubation, ventilate to keep pH 7.45 to 7.55 and avoid respiratory acidosis, which worsens cardiotoxicity.
Activated charcoal 50 g within 1 hour of ingestion only if the airway is protected.
Hypotension: crystalloid boluses and sodium bicarbonate, then a direct-acting vasopressor (noradrenaline) if still hypotensive.

sections.title: Sodium bicarbonate
items: Indications: QRS above 100 ms, ventricular arrhythmia, hypotension not responding to fluids, or seizures with ECG changes.
Give 8.4% sodium bicarbonate 1 to 2 mEq/kg (1 to 2 mL/kg) IV over a few minutes; repeat every few minutes until the QRS narrows and BP improves.
Target arterial pH 7.45 to 7.55; do not exceed about 7.55. Check blood gas, sodium and potassium frequently (alkalosis causes hypokalaemia).
Once stable, maintain alkalaemia with further boluses or an infusion guided by ECG and pH; hyperventilation can be used in ventilated patients who cannot tolerate more sodium or fluid.
Hypertonic saline is an alternative sodium load when alkalosis limits further bicarbonate.

sections.title: Arrhythmias, seizures and refractory toxicity
items: Ventricular tachycardia: sodium bicarbonate first; lidocaine 1 to 1.5 mg/kg IV if refractory. Avoid class IA (procainamide) and IC (flecainide) antiarrhythmics and amiodarone.
Seizures: benzodiazepines (lorazepam 2 to 4 mg IV or diazepam 10 mg IV); give bicarbonate as seizure-induced acidosis worsens cardiotoxicity. Do not use phenytoin.
Refractory shock or arrhythmia despite bicarbonate and vasopressors: consider VA-ECMO where available; lipid emulsion (20%, 1.5 mL/kg) has weak evidence. In cardiac arrest continue prolonged CPR.
Haemodialysis and haemoperfusion are not recommended: TCAs are not dialysable (EXTRIP).

sections.title: Monitoring and disposition
items: Continuous ECG and BP; repeat 12-lead ECGs and blood gases while on bicarbonate.
Asymptomatic patients with a normal ECG and normal mental state 6 hours after ingestion can be medically cleared, then psychiatric assessment.
Symptomatic patients: HDU or ICU until the ECG has normalised and they are clinically stable off bicarbonate.
Anticholinergic delirium may persist for days; manage with benzodiazepines and nursing care.

sections.title: Pitfalls
items: Physostigmine for anticholinergic delirium in TCA overdose: risk of bradycardia and asystole.
Flumazenil in a mixed benzodiazepine and TCA overdose: precipitates seizures.
Phenytoin or class IA/IC antiarrhythmics, which worsen sodium channel blockade.
Allowing acidosis from hypoventilation or seizures.
Relying on a urine TCA immunoassay: many drugs (carbamazepine, antipsychotics, antihistamines) cross-react.

drugs.name: Sodium bicarbonate 8.4%
drugs.dose: 1 to 2 mEq/kg (1 to 2 mL/kg) IV bolus, repeated until QRS narrows
drugs.notes: Target pH 7.45 to 7.55; monitor sodium and potassium.

drugs.name: Lorazepam
drugs.dose: 2 to 4 mg IV (0.1 mg/kg, max 4 mg), repeat once

drugs.name: Noradrenaline (norepinephrine)
drugs.dose: Start 0.05 to 0.1 mcg/kg/min IV, titrate to MAP 65 mmHg
